The Ethereum price plunged below the psychological support at $2000 and, since then, is struggling to hold the $1900 price range

Ethereum's decline is being driven by several factors, including ETF withdrawals, selling by large holders and heavy liquidations in the derivatives market.

The $1,829 support level is now critical for ETH. If buyers fail to defend it, the price could slide towards $1,725, while a recovery above $2,000 would offer some relief.

The Ethereum price is struggling to regain the $2,000 level as selling pressure continues to weigh on the broader market. Persistent outflows from spot Ethereum ETFs, reported sales from wallets linked to the Ethereum Foundation, and large whale transactions have added to concerns about investor confidence. The decline has also been accompanied by rising liquidations in the derivatives market, putting leveraged traders under pressure.

However, the sell-off is not the only story surrounding ETH. Network activity remains substantial, raising questions about the disconnect between Ethereum’s underlying usage and its recent market performance. With derivatives positioning weakening and institutional flows under scrutiny, can ETH stabilise and reclaim $2,000, or is another leg lower ahead?

Institutional withdrawals have emerged as one of the major sources of selling pressure on Ethereum. US spot Ethereum ETFs recorded approximately $695.9 million in net outflows during November, with withdrawals reported in seven of the month’s first eight trading sessions. The trend continued on November 13, when the funds registered another net outflow of around $64.95 million.

Besides, on-chain activity has added to the concerns. A wallet identified by blockchain trackers as linked to the Ethereum Foundation sold another 2,000 ETH, worth approximately $3.87 million, on November 13. The wallet’s reported sales since October 26 had reached 6,785 ETH by that date. Lookonchain subsequently reported another 1,000 ETH sale on November 14, taking its tracked sales over the preceding five days to 5,000 ETH.

The #EthereumFoundation-linked wallet (0x5CBC) dumped another 1,000 $ETH($1.9M) an hour ago.Over the past 5 days, this wallet has sold 5,000 $ETH ($9.92M) at an average price of $1,983.5.https://t.co/LpNlrLUUAO pic.twitter.com/lgeVlj6AfJ

The wider whale activity is not entirely one-sided. One large holder reportedly swapped 16,700 ETH for approximately $30.94 million in USDT, while another whale accumulated 10,380 ETH, worth nearly $19.91 million, despite carrying substantial unrealised losses. These transactions point to different strategies among large holders rather than a uniform move towards selling. Still, the combination of sustained ETF withdrawals and sizeable ETH disposals has added to the market’s cautious sentiment as the token struggles below $2,000.

Ethereum’s derivatives market is showing that traders are becoming more cautious as the price struggles to recover. Open interest across exchanges has dropped to approximately $23.08 billion, down 3.85% over 24 hours. Besides, $241.41 million in ETH positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours, with long positions accounting for approximately 76% of the total.

Funding rates, meanwhile, have moved close to neutral at around 0.0001%. This suggests that the earlier preference for long positions has largely faded, leaving bullish and bearish traders more evenly positioned. Futures activity remains considerably higher than spot trading, with 24-hour futures volume at approximately $47.33 billion compared with $3.10 billion in spot volume. This highlights how heavily ETH trading continues to rely on the derivatives market.

Ethereum’s daily chart continues to show signs of weakness, with the latest decline pushing ETH further below its moving averages. The bearish alignment of the EMA ribbon reflects the loss of upward momentum. A confirmed death cross, where the 50-day EMA moves below the 200-day EMA, would add another warning that the broader trend is turning increasingly bearish.

The order blocks also highlight how sellers have been gaining ground. Instead of facing resistance at one fixed level, Ethereum has encountered successive selling zones at progressively lower prices. Each recovery attempt has struggled to move through these areas, suggesting that sellers are stepping in earlier and making it harder for buyers to regain control. The latest drop below $1,900 adds to this pressure and leaves the market looking vulnerable.

Ethereum is facing pressure from multiple sides, with persistent ETF outflows, reported large-holder sales and a wave of long liquidations weighing on market sentiment. The derivatives market also shows traders scaling back their positions, while the daily chart points to a weakening price structure. The successive lower order blocks suggest that sellers are defending increasingly lower levels, making a sustained recovery more difficult.

For now, $1,829 remains the key support to watch. A breakdown below this level could expose ETH to further losses towards $1,725, while a recovery above $2,000 would be an early sign that buyers are returning. However, ETH needs to overcome the overhead selling zones and improve its broader moving-average structure before the bullish outlook can gain traction. Until then, the risk of another leg lower remains.

#5175. Why Is Crypto Crashing Today? Bitcoin Falls Below $73K as Zcash (ZEC) Leads Crypto Losses

Why is crypto crashing? A hot CPI report raised Fed hike bets. ZEC fell below $1,000, the worst of 20 large coins this week.

Why is crypto crashing on Wednesday, November 11? The sell-off that began with Tuesday’s hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation report has carried into today, and almost every major coin is lower.

Bitcoin (BTC) dropped below $73,000 on Tuesday, touching $72,727 on Binance, and now trades at about $73,800. Ether (ETH) briefly slipped to $2,006, while XRP and Solana (SOL) are down 2% to 3% in 24 hours. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a daily gauge of market mood from 0 to 100, has fallen to 29.

The report changed what traders expect from the Federal Reserve. Bond yields jumped, and bets on a larger December rate hike nearly tripled within two hours.

One coin is falling much harder than the rest. Zcash (ZEC) is a cryptocurrency launched in 2016 that lets users hide the sender, the receiver and the amount of a payment. It dropped below $1,000 on Wednesday for the first time since September 5. ZEC now trades at about $966, down 15.4% in 24 hours and 24.8% in a week.

ZEC has been one of this year’s best performers. It rose from about $526 on January 1 to a closing high of $1,653 on September 26. We checked the 20 largest coins on Binance, and ZEC fell the most over both the day and the week, even though it is still up 89% in 2026.

Trader 0x8742 opened a 10x long on 18,000 $ZEC ($17.63M) and is now down over $2.8M.

Liquidation price: $895.46.https://t.co/azzt3xvmay pic.twitter.com/wczndt7doC

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 11, 2026

So why are the markets spooked, and why is ZEC taking the hardest hit?

Inflation came in hot. The consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast.

That reading crossed a line the Fed had drawn. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech hours before the report that core inflation of about 0.3% would make a half-point hike in December worth considering.

Traders took him at his word. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 0.5 percentage point or more in December went from 4.4% just before the report to 12.8% two hours later. They sit at 9.4% now, while a standard quarter-point hike is priced at 85.5%.

Higher rates hurt crypto in a simple way. They make cash and bonds pay more, so money flows out of riskier bets. On Tuesday, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose from 4.86% to 4.98%.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

ZEC had the most to give back. We compared the price changes of 20 large coins on Binance over the past week and since January 1.

When markets get nervous, traders tend to sell what has made them the most money. ZEC has fallen 41% from its September 26 closing high of $1,653.

Borrowed money made the drop faster. On Hyperliquid, ZEC fell from $1,199.20 to $965.79 in less than a day. Lookonchain counted 32 traders holding more than $1 million each in leveraged bets on a rising ZEC price. Of those, 27 are now losing money, with about $23.7 million in paper losses between them.

Sharp drops have not always lasted. Since January 2025, ZEC has fallen 12% or more in a single day 14 times on Binance. Seven days later, it was higher eight times, with a median gain of 6.5%.

EXPLORE: Fed Meeting Today: Traders Price a 95% Hold and a 79% December Hike. What Does It Mean for Crypto?

ZEC trades at about $966. It touched $961.07 on Wednesday, its lowest price since September 4.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, ZEC has fallen below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $1,200.68. It is still above its 200-day EMA at $872.23.

For Bitcoin, the line to watch is Tuesday’s low of $72,727. Below that, $68,902, the August 20 low, is the next support.

So, why is crypto crashing? A hot inflation report raised the odds of a bigger Fed hike, and ZEC’s leveraged bulls are paying the most for it. A daily close back above $1,050 would be the first sign the selling is easing.

The daily trading volume of the NVDA-USDC perpetual contract on the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid has reached a record $2.14 billion, according to CoinGlass. The contract is provided by the Trade.xyz protocol, and only Bitcoin had higher trading volume on Hyperliquid over the same period.

Nvidia futures also surpassed Ethereum, Solana and XRP in trading volume, and the combined volume of Nvidia derivatives across all tracked crypto exchanges reached $9.51 billion, according to CoinGlass.

The latest surge in trading comes amid the resignation of Jensen Huang, the co-founder of Nvidia and the only CEO in the history of the company. Huang stepped down on Nov. 12 amid an internal investigation, and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO.

On Nasdaq, the price of NVDA went down by as much as 14% during the day, but the stock later recovered most of the loss and closed at $166.19, down 4.34%.

Sharp price moves cost leveraged traders on crypto exchanges $40.86 million, according to CoinGlass. Of that amount, $26.23 million came from the on-chain ticker XYZ:NVDA, and $14.63 million came from the base NVDA contract. The largest single liquidation on Hyperliquid was a $1.54 million long position.

In the base NVDA contract, $8.87 million in long positions and $5.89 million in short positions were liquidated. During the same period, the price of Nvidia futures on crypto exchanges went up by 5.6% to $171.17.

Liquidations in the NVDA contracts were almost twice as large as those in XRP, where traders lost $20.75 million over the same period. The price of XRP went down by 2.5% to $1.0192, and long positions accounted for 94.5% of XRP liquidations, or $19.6 million.

The liquidations came amid a sell-off across major cryptocurrencies. The price of Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 to $69,450.50, down 5.3% over 24 hours, and Ethereum fell 4.1% to $1,958.71.

Over the past 24 hours, crypto exchanges liquidated 187,389 traders for a total of $1.65 billion, and 88% of that amount came from long positions, according to CoinGlass. Bitcoin traders lost the most at $919.56 million, followed by Ethereum traders at $297.24 million.

Finally, Nvidia is expected to report its quarterly earnings on Nov. 17.

#5170. Bank of America Warns of 50 bps Fed Hike in December: Is Bitcoin Heading for Another 2022-Style Drop?

Bank of America (BofA) says hot CPI puts a 50bps December Fed hike on the table. BTC fell a week later after 5 of the last 6 big hikes.

Bank of America said this week that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates by half a percentage point in December. The warning came after Tuesday’s October inflation report ran hotter than expected for a third month in a row. In Bitcoin news, the coin trades at $73,888 on Binance, down 0.6% in 24 hours. It dropped to $72,727 on Tuesday after the report, its lowest price since August 20.

The bank still expects the Fed to raise rates by 0.25 percentage points, or 25 basis points (bps), at its December 8–9 meeting. But it says the case for a bigger move is growing, and it calls the Fed’s decision to hold rates in October a possible policy mistake.

Traders are starting to listen. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 50 bps or more in December rose from 0.6% on Monday to 11.4% on Wednesday.

BANK OF AMERICA WARNS FED COULD DELIVER 50BPS HIKE IN DECEMBER

Bank of America says October's hot CPI report virtually guarantees a December Fed rate hike — and opens the door to a larger 50bps move.

Headline CPI rose 0.4%, while core CPI climbed 0.3%, marking a third…

— *Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaone) November 11, 2026

The bank’s call rests on three months of hot data. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, and core prices, which leave out food and energy because they swing the most, rose 0.3%. Both beat forecasts, the third upside surprise in a row in the Bureau of Labor Statistics report.

Bank of America now estimates that core PCE inflation, the Fed’s preferred measure, is running at 3.3% a year. The Fed’s target is 2%. The bank says price rises are spreading from goods to services, with electronics, airfares and hotels leading the increases.

Its base case is still a 25 bps hike in December. The change is in the risks: a 50 bps move is now possible, and the bank sees a growing chance of another hike in January instead of March.

The bank is not alone. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech on Tuesday morning that he leans toward a 25 bps hike in December. If core inflation came in around 0.3% again, he said, a 50 bps hike “should be considered.” It did.

Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more. That tends to pull money out of risky assets like BTC, and a faster pace of hikes pulls harder.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

The size of the hike has mattered for BTC. We measured Bitcoin’s price on Binance from the 2 p.m. ET announcement of each Fed rate hike since 2022 to one week later. That covers 12 hikes: six of 50 bps or more and six of 25 bps.

After the six big hikes, BTC was lower a week later five times. The median move was a 6% drop. The worst came after the 50 bps hike in May 2022, when BTC fell 23% in a week.

After the six 25 bps hikes, the picture was milder. BTC was lower a week later four times, but the median move was a drop of just 0.6%.

The record comes with a caveat. All six big hikes happened in 2022, a bear market that also saw the collapses of Terra in May and FTX in November. Those crashes made the falls after the May and November hikes worse.

The most recent hike was a 25 bps move on September 16. BTC rose 11.3% in the week after it, as the uncertainty that had built up before the meeting cleared. That makes the size of December’s hike, more than the hike itself, the Bitcoin news to watch.

DISCOVER: Bitcoin CPI Reaction: 10 of 13 Cool Inflation Reports Triggered an Hourly Gain – Can Inflation Data Reverse the Downtrend?

BTC trades at $73,888, down 0.6% in 24 hours and 5.8% over the past week. It sits below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight, on the daily chart. The 50-day EMA stands at $78,897 and the 200-day EMA at $76,449.

For Bitcoin news, the next test is the Fed’s own message. Traders already expect a 25 bps hike. If more officials join Waller and Bank of America in backing 50 bps, BTC may have to defend $72,727 before the December 9 decision.

According to Lunde, the daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) for Bitcoin has fallen to 25, which shows that the market has become oversold.

Bitcoin has fallen below $68,000, extending its decline to more than 20% from its October highs.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $1.91 billion in net outflows over seven consecutive trading sessions.

Nearly $1.5 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated in 24 hours, increasing the risk of further downside.

Bitcoin price has plunged toward $65,000, raising fresh concerns about whether BTC could crash toward $60,000. The latest sell-off has pushed Bitcoin below $68,000, while ETF outflows and heavy liquidations continue to weaken market demand. With BTC approaching a critical support zone after several consecutive weekly losses, investors are watching for signs of a reversal. Is Bitcoin heading toward $60K, or can buyers stop the decline?

Bitcoin’s breakdown below $68,000 has shifted the market’s attention toward lower support levels. The cryptocurrency dropped below $66,000 on November 14, reaching its weakest level since August as selling pressure continued through the weekend.

The decline has also extended Bitcoin’s losing streak, putting it on course for a sixth consecutive weekly loss. From its October highs near $86,000, BTC has now surrendered a substantial portion of its gains.

Macroeconomic concerns are adding to the pressure. Hotter US inflation has strengthened expectations of further Federal Reserve rate increases, while a stronger dollar and rising Treasury yields have reduced appetite for riskier assets. That combination leaves Bitcoin vulnerable as investors reassess their exposure to speculative investments.

Institutional demand is becoming another major concern for Bitcoin investors. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $185.45 million in net outflows on November 13, extending their withdrawal streak to seven consecutive trading sessions.

The cumulative outflows reached roughly $1.91 billion between November 5 and November 13. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for a significant portion of the withdrawals, highlighting the scale of institutional selling pressure.

However, the broader ETF picture is not entirely negative. Despite the recent withdrawals, cumulative net inflows across US spot Bitcoin ETFs remained above $54 billion, with total net assets around $86.2 billion.

The immediate concern is whether persistent redemptions will continue to weaken demand. If ETF withdrawals extend into another week, Bitcoin could struggle to attract enough buying interest to establish a durable recovery.

Bitcoin’s decline has also triggered a major wave of forced selling across the derivatives market. Approximately $1.5 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, with bullish positions accounting for the overwhelming majority.

Bitcoin positions represented a substantial share of those liquidations. When leveraged long positions are forcibly closed, exchanges sell the underlying exposure, potentially accelerating an existing decline.

This creates additional pressure during periods of weak liquidity. Traders who expected Bitcoin to recover are being forced out of positions, while fresh buyers remain cautious about entering before the market stabilizes.

Bitcoin price is approaching a critical technical zone after losing the $70,000 and $68,000 levels. The price action shows a sustained downward trend, with lower highs and lower lows indicating that sellers remain in control.

The $64,000–$68,000 region is now an important demand zone. If buyers defend this area and push BTC back above $68,000–$70,000, the cryptocurrency could attempt a short-term recovery. However, a sustained breakdown below $64,000 would expose the next major support near $60,000–$61,000. That level could become the market’s next significant test if selling pressure continues.

On the upside, Bitcoin needs to reclaim $70,000 before a stronger recovery can take shape. The $75,000–$77,000 region remains a broader resistance zone that buyers would need to overcome to improve the technical outlook.

Japanese tech and fintech conglomerate Rakuten Group is among the institutional holders of a U.S. spot XRP ETF, according to the company's latest 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Rakuten also holds funds tracking Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana, and these positions were worth roughly $6.42 million combined at the end of the quarter on Sept. 30, 2026.

The filing shows that Rakuten held 6,690 shares of the Bitwise XRP ETF worth $111,255. At press time, the price of XRP stands at $1.03, and the shares of the Bitwise fund trade at $11.51, according to SoSoValue, so the XRP ETF stake of Rakuten is now worth about $77,000.

Rakuten is not the only institutional investor in the new XRP funds, and Raymond James Financial has also disclosed positions in spot XRP ETFs, according to SEC filings.

The largest position of Rakuten is in BlackRock's spot Bitcoin fund, the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF, and Rakuten held $5,893,593 worth of its shares at the end of the third quarter. Besides, Rakuten owns $263,632 of the iShares Ethereum Trust ETF and $150,728 of the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF.

U.S. rules require any institutional manager holding more than $100 million in U.S. exchange-listed securities to disclose its portfolio every quarter, no matter where it's based. Stellar (XLM), the blockchain co-founded by Jed McCaleb, has become the leader in daily market cap growth for tokenized real-world asset (RWA) funds, according to Token Terminal data published by the RWA Foundation. Over the 24 hours to Nov. 13, the market cap of tokenized funds on Stellar went up by $44.9 million, and the network surpassed both Ethereum and Solana.

Over the same period, the market cap of tokenized funds on Solana, Ethereum and zkSync Era increased by $29 million, $10.8 million and $3.5 million, respectively.

Stellar is currently the second-largest blockchain for tokenized funds after Ethereum, according to Token Terminal. Over the past year, the RWA market on Stellar has grown roughly sixfold and reached $4.67 billion, according to rwa.xyz. At press time, the price of XLM stands at $0.1476.

According to the Stellar Development Foundation, Stellar was designed with the requirements of banks and transfer agents in mind. In this context, the compliance tools are built into the base layer of the network, and an issuer can vet investors through trustlines, freeze accounts and claw back assets.

Transactions on Stellar settle in 3 to 5 seconds, and the fees on the network are measured in fractions of a cent. Besides, users can move funds to and from fiat currencies through local providers, which are called anchors on Stellar.

Franklin Templeton's BENJI money market fund has run on Stellar since 2021, and it was the first U.S. mutual fund on a public blockchain.

Today, Spiko, Ondo and WisdomTree are also building their own funds and tokenized U.S. Treasuries on Stellar. Spiko offers euro funds managed by Amundi, and Ondo has launched its USDY token on the network.

In May 2026, DTCC and the Stellar Development Foundation announced that the Depository Trust Company (DTC) will tokenize the assets it holds in custody on Stellar. According to DTCC, DTC-tokenized assets are expected to become available on the network in the first half of 2027.

On Nov. 12, DTCC also announced that it will connect its tokenization service to Solana in the second half of 2027.

On-chain metrics from reputated dashboards like CryptoQuant, CoinGlass, and even TradingView reveal a clear divergence in Bitcoin holder behavior during the November 2026 market correction.

Following a failed late-September rally to $87,153, Bitcoin dropped to the $65,800–$66,083 support zone. While short-term traders and spot ETFs are actively liquidating positions, long-term investors are absorbing the downturn with minimal panic selling.

Current Bitcoin holder behavior shows structural resilience among experienced investors despite immediate spot price weakness.

Tracking Bitcoin holder behavior requires examining total supply held by wallets inactive for over 155 days.

According to CoinGlass data as of November 11, 2026, Long-Term Holder Supply holds steady at 16.24 million BTC.

Rather than distributing into the late-September bounce to $87,153, older cohorts retained their coins, allowing mid-2026 purchases to mature into the long-term bracket.

The Long-Term Holder Spent Output Profit Ratio (LTH-SOPR) currently reads 0.90. Readings below 1.0 confirm that the small fraction of older coins moving on-chain are doing so at a slight loss.

Simultaneously, Supply-Adjusted Coin Days Destroyed (CDD) sits at a subdued 0.94, well below the August 2026 spike above 3.0. Older coins remain largely dormant, proving that conviction holders are not driving the November sell-off.

Recent market entrants display reactive Bitcoin holder behavior during price drawdowns. The Short-Term Holder SOPR (STH-SOPR) dropped from above 1.02 in October to 0.96 in mid-November.

When STH-SOPR fails to hold 1.0 as support, it signals that traders who bought between 1 hour and 155 days ago are exiting at a loss, adding direct downward momentum to spot markets.

The broader market’s Net Unrealized Profit/Loss (NUPL) has compressed to 0.21, placing the network in the lower hope/fear zone.

Historically, NUPL readings near 0.21 indicate that most excess speculative profit has been wiped out. Because aggregate unrealized gains are low, long-term investors have little financial incentive to distribute coins at $65,836.

Exchange flow data confirms that spot selling pressure is stabilizing rather than accelerating. Total Exchange Inflow dropped to 8.1K BTC, while Total Exchange Outflow sits slightly higher at 9.3K BTC.

Net outflows during a price drop indicate that buyers are withdrawing coins to cold storage rather than depositing them onto trading platforms for liquidation.

Analyzing Bitcoin holder behavior alongside institutional flows highlights the primary cause of the November crash.

The 30-day ETF Demand Growth and Apparent Demand metrics have plunged deep into negative territory, reaching roughly -200K BTC in combined apparent demand contraction.

Without institutional ETF inflows to absorb routine selling, even modest retail capitulation pushed price down through moving average supports toward the $65,670–$66,083 horizontal zone.

Note on How to Read This Table: On-chain metrics often reflect two different timeframes at once. The Bearish column shows what is hurting Bitcoin’s price right now (active selling and weak demand), while the Bullish column shows why those exact conditions historically help form a long-term price bottom.

So to keep it simple, the current Bitcoin holder behavior reflects long-term accumulation paired with short-term institutional and retail distribution. Long-term holders are not distributing at $65,800; they hold 16.24 million BTC and keep older coins dormant.

Instead, the drop from $87,153 stems from negative 30-day ETF demand growth and short-term holders selling at a loss. If Bitcoin holds the $65,670–$66,083 support level while exchange outflows continue exceeding inflows, current conditions align with structural bottom formation rather than cycle-top distribution.

#5149. Strategy Sends Crucial Message on Bitcoin's Quantum Security

Strategy, the world's largest corporate Bitcoin (BTC) holder, has sent an important message regarding Bitcoin’s future resistance to quantum computing attacks.

The company, which was co-founded by renowned Bitcoin champion Michael Saylor, recently posted on X that the Bitcoin network can implement new security measures as and when they are needed.

“Quantum-resistant upgrades can be adopted if & when it's needed,” wrote Strategy.

These comments come at a time when the crypto industry is debating whether the rise of quantum computing could, in the long run, threaten Bitcoin’s cryptographic security.

Given that Bitcoin leverages elliptic curve cryptography for transaction security, quantum computing could pose a significant threat to Bitcoin.

A sufficiently powerful quantum computer has the potential to reverse-engineer private keys from exposed public keys. This could give attackers access to the Bitcoin holdings associated with those keys.

At this point, there is no known publicly available quantum computer that can successfully break Bitcoin’s cryptography in this manner.

While speaking at the World Bank in Washington in October, Saylor said that the Bitcoin network would be able to defend itself against any realistic quantum computing threat by coming together and upgrading the software.

Saylor estimated that such an upgrade would take about 90 days once a worldwide consensus is reached on the need for quantum-resistant cryptography.

Saylor also warned against the hasty introduction of new cryptography. He reasoned that more complex security measures may themselves introduce weaknesses.

However, the 90-day estimate has come under scrutiny because such a network-wide shift would involve developers agreeing on technical changes and Bitcoin users moving their funds to new, secure addresses.

Interestingly, Strategy has also initiated efforts aimed at research and development for Bitcoin’s long-term security.

In July, Strategy was part of a group of seven major financial institutions and crypto companies, including BlackRock and Coinbase, that formed the Bitcoin Security Consortium.

The Bitcoin Security Consortium has committed $15 million over three years. One of the areas of focus of the consortium is post-quantum cryptography.

In fact, Bitcoin developers are already working on ways to address the quantum computing issue.

One of the most prominent proposals is Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 360 (BIP-360). This BIP introduces a new type of transaction output, Pay-to-Merkle-Root (P2MR).

The Cardano founder acknowledged that the network’s early focus on emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, liquid non-custodial staking, and the need for Layer-2 (L2) solutions built around its Extended UTXO (EUTXO) model, came in handy during the hacking incident.

Unlike traditional staking models that lock up assets, Cardano’s liquid staking allows holders to delegate their ADA while retaining full control. As a result, they can spend, transfer, or move their funds without first having to unstake them.

Therefore, this approach is unique because it combines network participation with financial flexibility while supporting a decentralized pool ecosystem. Additionally, it reduces reliance on centralized custodians, boosting the network’s broader resilience.

The crypto market crash deepens as $1B+ in longs get liquidated. Bitcoin sits mid-range at $72,969; fear at 28 isn’t a bottom yet.

Bitcoin fell below $73,000 on Thursday, November 12, extending a week-long crypto market crash in which traders who bet on a rebound were forced out of their positions again and again.

Bitcoin touched $72,735 on Binance, a hair above Tuesday’s $72,727 low and its weakest price since August 20. It trades at $72,969, down 9.4% from the November 4 close.

BREAKING: $BTC just fell to its lowest level since August.

Over $210 million worth of longs liquidated in the past 24 hours.

The dumping continues… pic.twitter.com/R7NVGivFnD

— Crypto Rover (@cryptorover) November 12, 2026

The altcoins are doing worse. Over seven days, Ethereum has lost 16.4%, Solana 14.7% and XRP 21.3%. CoinGecko values the whole crypto market at $2.42 trillion on Thursday, and Bitcoin makes up 60.5% of it.

Leverage made every drop bigger. More than $1 billion of bets were liquidated on Monday alone, almost all of them longs, the positions that profit only if prices rise. Liquidation means the exchange closes a trade by force once the trader’s collateral runs out, and those forced sales push the price down further.

So is this the flush that ends the crypto market slide, or is there more to come? The data has an answer, and it is not a comforting one.

The sell-off had no single cause. Four pieces of bad news landed one after another:

Each hit forced out more leveraged longs across the crypto market. Thursday’s slide continued the pattern on a smaller scale. We added up every forced closure in Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP and Dogecoin futures on OKX, one of the largest exchanges, over the past 24 hours. Longs lost $27.6 million, against $12.3 million for shorts.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Slides Toward $73K as Nvidia Plunges 9% and MSCI Drops Saylor’s Strategy

Big liquidations usually clear out the crowd. This time, the crowd came back.

In plain terms, traders keep buying every dip with borrowed money. That leaves fuel for another round of forced selling if Bitcoin drops through the next support. Bottoms tend to come when funding turns negative and open interest falls hard, a sign that leveraged buyers have given up.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Next Crypto to Hit 1 Dollar

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, which scores market mood from 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed), reads 28 today. Fear is usually read as a buy signal. The history says it is not enough on its own.

We checked every day since February 2018 when the index sat at 28 or lower, 943 days in all, and where Bitcoin stood later.

This year’s two bottoms came with real panic. When Bitcoin hit $60,000 on February 6, the index read 9. When it bottomed at $57,800 on July 1, it read 11. Today’s 28 is fear, but it is not capitulation, the moment sellers give up all at once.

On the weekly chart, where each candle covers one week, Bitcoin has spent 2026 in a wide range. The low is $57,800 from July 1 and the high is $87,396 from late September. The midpoint is $72,598, almost exactly where Bitcoin trades now.

The price lost its 50-week exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $78,219. Its 200-week EMA sits at $69,597. Bitcoin closed below that line for 16 weeks this year, in February and March and again from June to mid-August, and both of the year’s bottoms formed during those stretches.

For the crypto market, three signs would say the bottom is close: the fear index dropping toward the teens, funding turning negative, and open interest falling as longs give up. None has shown up yet. Until they do, the 200-week EMA at $69,597 is the line that separates a pullback inside the 2026 range from a retest of the summer lows.

#5146. Nakamoto Sells More Bitcoin (BTC)

As per its latest quarterly financials, David Bailey's Bitcoin treasury firm Nakamoto Inc. (NASDAQ: NAKA) has sold an additional 184 BTC from its Bitcoin stash.

Nakamoto Inc., a firm that built its corporate strategy around Bitcoin, held a total of 4,283 BTC as of Sept. 30. The figure is down from 4,467 BTC at the end of June.

Bitcoin Treasuries data shows that Nakamoto Inc. sold 184 BTC in the third quarter of 2026. The firm now has a total of 4,283 BTC in its Bitcoin stash. Nakamoto currently sits in 21st place on the Bitcoin 100 corporate treasury rankings.

The recent company filing indicates that Nakamoto Inc. generated around $13.2 million in proceeds from digital asset sales in the third quarter. However, the filing does not appear to specify whether the 184 BTC were sold in a single transaction.

Nakamoto currently holds approximately $357.9 million worth of Bitcoin despite selling more BTC in the latest period.

This is not the first time in 2026 that David Bailey's firm has reduced its Bitcoin stash.

In March, Nakamoto Inc. sold around 284 BTC worth $20 million to meet working capital needs and fund operations following its acquisitions of BTC Inc. and UTXO Management.

Nakamoto sold its BTC at an average price of around $70,422 per Bitcoin. That was far less than its original Bitcoin purchase price.

In the first quarter, Nakamoto Inc. also received a premium of around 43 BTC from its derivatives strategies before selling around 40 BTC.

Nakamoto Inc. also sold a large chunk of Bitcoin in June.

The company sold around 600 BTC for 35.6 million USDT, as per the company's second-quarter financials.

Combined with proceeds from certain Bitcoin derivative positions, the company generated around $48 million from those transactions.

Nakamoto Inc. used $45 million of that sum to partially repay its Bitcoin-backed loan from cryptocurrency exchange Kraken, reducing its principal amount from 210 million USDT to 165 million USDT.

The recent Bitcoin sell-off comes as Nakamoto continues working to meet its substantial debt obligations while expanding its business operations.

It had roughly 3,030 BTC pledged as collateral for debt as of Sept. 30. That left 1,253 BTC unpledged.

On Nov. 11, Nakamoto Inc. extended the maturity of a 60 million USDT loan from Kraken by one year. The company moved the loan maturity date from December 2026 to December 2027. Nakamoto currently has no remaining principal maturities in 2026.

#5145. Trezor slashes reseller network by 80% following hardware implant discovery – Details

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Trezor confirmed on the 12th of November that three Safe 5 hardware wallets sold by CryptoBilis contained malicious implants. Fortunately, no customer had reported losing funds.

Still, Trezor urged affected buyers to move their crypto after releasing a firmware fix.

Customers bought those 3 devices between the 20th of August and the 23rd of September through CryptoBilis directly or its Tokopedia and Shopee stores. Trezor examined one device in its lab and identified two more from customer photos.

48 buyers had contacted the company, and at press time, checks were ongoing. Trezor reported that there were no confirmed cases involving other models or resellers.

Apparently, the implants could take recovery phrases and passphrases that appeared on the wallet screen.

On X, a user asked how a software update could stop a physical implant from recording the display. Trezor explained that firmware could “listen to the communication between the MCU and the display,” and the firm has now changed the order of commands needed for the trigger.

Regardless, Trezor still urged buyers to use a fresh recovery phrase because “the update can’t protect a wallet backup that was captured before it.” This advice applied to customers who bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis from March 2026 onward.

The hardware wallet company also urged those using its devices to move funds to a new wallet with a fresh recovery phrase. It told buyers with unused devices to leave them unconfigured. Eligible buyers could contact Trezor Support for a replacement or a refund where shipping limited their options.

Trezor dropped CryptoBilis on the 9th of October after reports of tampered Ledger devices sold through them. A customer also flagged a suspected Safe 5 implant on the 28th of October.

Trezor issued a warning two days later, saying that it cut its reseller network by about 80% and tightened rules on sourcing, storage, and access.

This brought the debate back to what self-custody protects, and as Ledger CEO Pascal Gauthier said,

Everybody will be hacked at some point. Perfect security doesn’t exist.

#5143. Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO After Second Affair Bombshell: Who Is Colette Kress?

Following Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO, who is the Apple exec being tipped for the permanent role, and how has the NVDA price reacted?

Today (November 12, 2026), Nvidia announced that co-founder and longtime CEO Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and Board member, effective immediately.

The decision follows intense scrutiny over personal and potential national-security-related controversies. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been appointed Interim CEO while remaining CFO. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aioLZFt2Xwc The board has also named longtime director Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever Chair and launched a search for a permanent successor, with a high-profile Apple exec tipped as an early frontrunner.

Nvidia shares reacted sharply, falling more than -10% in premarket trading and extending recent losses that have erased hundreds of billions in market value. As of midday trading, NVDA was fluctuating near the mid-$150s to low-$160s range.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly has a second affair on top of the suspected Chinese spy.He also had a romantic relationship with Kimberly Powell, someone who worked at Nvidia since 2008, according to a New York Times report. pic.twitter.com/QJRTnJb8c6— Pubity (@pubity) November 11, 2026

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly has a second affair on top of the suspected Chinese spy.He also had a romantic relationship with Kimberly Powell, someone who worked at Nvidia since 2008, according to a New York Times report. pic.twitter.com/QJRTnJb8c6

The resignation stems from revelations of two extramarital affairs. The first involved Alice Huang, a businesswoman linked to the Singapore-based AI company Megaspeed, a significant Nvidia customer. US authorities have identified her as a suspected asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.

Reports indicated Huang had been photographed with her on multiple occasions, raising concerns about potential intelligence targeting of the Nvidia CEO.

Huang publicly apologized to employees for being unfaithful to his wife but denied compromising national security or company secrets. The situation escalated further when additional reporting alleged a second relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare and a direct report to Huang.

These dual revelations prompted Nvidia’s board to open an internal investigation and ultimately accept Huang’s resignation after a late-night meeting.

The combination of personal misconduct involving a subordinate and the national-security implications surrounding the alleged Chinese intelligence connection proved decisive.

https://twitter.com/JesseCohenInv/status/2120779503119012207 Colette Kress has served as Nvidia’s Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer since September 2013. Before joining the company, she spent nearly 25 years in senior finance roles at major technology firms,

These firms include Cisco (where she was CFO of the Business Technology and Operations organization) and Microsoft (where she was CFO of the Server and Tools division), as well as earlier positions at Texas Instruments.

She holds a bachelor’s degree in finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University. During her tenure as CFO, Nvidia’s revenue grew dramatically from roughly $4Bn to over $200Bn as the company became the dominant force in AI accelerators.

As Interim CEO, she is tasked with providing continuity while the board searches for a permanent replacement, with Apple’s Johny Srouji tipped as an early frontrunner. Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Reveals Upcoming Coinbase Listings

Hyperliquid offers leveraged perpetual contracts tied to Nvidia’s share price, allowing traders 24/7 exposure without holding actual shares. These instruments track the underlying stock closely and have seen heavy volume during the scandal.

Since the initial reports of the affair and board investigation emerged in early November, the Hyperliquid NVDA perpetual has mirrored the traditional stock’s sharp decline.

The mark price has dropped from near or above $170–$175 to the mid-$150s, settling around $158–$160 by November 12, representing roughly a 9–11% decline in the most recent sessions alone and larger cumulative losses from pre-scandal highs.

Open interest has remained elevated (hundreds of millions of dollars), reflecting active speculative positioning, while funding rates have fluctuated as longs and shorts adjust.

Volume spiked significantly on the resignation news, consistent with forced liquidations and rapid repositioning. Technically, the contract has broken key short-term support levels, with momentum indicators deeply oversold in the near term.

Any stabilization in traditional NVDA stock would likely be reflected quickly on Hyperliquid, though the platform’s high-leverage environment amplifies both downside volatility and the potential magnitude of a bounce.

#5142. Binance recovers its stolen $6.3B – But U.S. authorities have frozen $2.7B already

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

After the largest hack in the history of crypto, Binance has announced that it has fully recovered all $6.3 billion in digital assets stolen during the cyberattack.

For those unaware, Binance initially recovered most of the stolen assets within days using company profits and emergency reserves, while the remaining 10% required additional time.

Well, the hack was so widespread that the operation involved more than 20,000 wallets and at least 65,000 transactions within a week, according to blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.

Of that, around $430,000 was also reportedly laundered through memecoins. Chainalysis also identified Chinese money-laundering networks as part of the cash conversion process.

But now Binance has made a complete comeback, and remarking on this 100% recovery, the exchange took to X and noted,

Once the zero-knowledge proof is generated, users can independently verify that their assets are backed at a minimum of 1:1.

To our users and community: thank you for your patience and understanding.

This coincided with Binance publishing an updated Proof of Reserves snapshot dated 12th November. According to reports, user BTC holdings rose 0.35% to 687,900 BTC, while ETH reserves increased 1.04% to 3.48 million ETH.

Meanwhile, BNB holdings also climbed 1.03% to 42.95 million tokens. However, USDT reserves declined 3.68% to 24.3 billion tokens.

However, the U.S. federal authorities and private-sector partners have frozen more than $2.7 billion in cryptocurrency stolen during the Binance cyberattack.

At the same time, the U.S. Department of Justice also secured court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in stolen assets as efforts to trace the remaining funds continue.

This further coincided with the U.S. Department of Justice’s announcement of coordinated actions against North Korean cybercriminal operations responsible for cryptocurrency thefts worth billions of dollars.

In fact, one major operation, called FaceStealer, has reportedly stolen more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the past 18 months.

Additionally, the FBI also seized cloud infrastructure used in the campaign and more than 900 webcam videos of victims.

More than $856.01 million in crypto liquidations happened with longs, equating to $771.7 million. Of the total liquidations, Bitcoin accounted for $454.7 million, with longs taking 96%.

As a result, BTC slid below $70,000 and was trading around $68,888, at press time, having lost 6% of its cap. A daily trading volume of $31.90 billion reinforced the sharp decline in price below $70,000.

For Ethereum [ETH], 91% of longs were liquidated from its total of $131.95 million. Other crypto assets saw over $218 million wiped out, with long positions representing 75%.

At the same time, a Bitcoin rebound toward $71,000 was becoming more fragile considering other factors. For instance, the market sentiment from some analysts, like Benjamin Cowen, was shifting.

This has been the case since the midterm US election results, implying investors were less optimistic as pro-crypto Republicans lost control of the house.

Additionally, monthly spot and futures demand was contracting at an accelerating rate. That of spot was at -280K BTC, while that of perpetual futures was at -82K, a total demand of -362K BTC.

Moreover, Bitcoin ETF outflows reached $300 million on the 11th of November and $48 million the following day. This indicated institutions were consistently withdrawing capital from Bitcoin and the crypto market in general. This adds institutional selling pressure to BTC.

This could be driven by renewed spot demand as its CVD is closer to neutral, though the improvement did not last there. The Futures taker CVD was dominated by sellers.

#5138. Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $69,000: Is the Worst Still to Come?

Bitcoin news: BTC hit $67,568 as longs were liquidated. Fear is Extreme, but BTC fell further after 15 of 16 past readings.

In Bitcoin news on Friday, November 13, the BTC USD price fell as low as $67,568 on Binance as a wave of forced selling wiped out leveraged bets on a rebound. It was the cryptocurrency’s lowest price since August 19.

Bitcoin trades at $68,772, down 6.7% in 24 hours and 9.1% in a week. Ether lost 5.5% and Solana 3.4% on the day.

BREAKING: Bitcoin falls below $69,000 and ETH nears $1,900 as selling pressure accelerates in crypto.

Crypto markets have now lost -$150 billion in 48 hours. pic.twitter.com/29QW0khxOh

— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) November 13, 2026

Most of the damage came from liquidations, when an exchange closes a leveraged trade by force once the trader’s collateral runs out. CoinGlass data cited by several outlets put the 24-hour total at about $1.4 billion, close to 90% of it from longs, the bets that prices would rise. Those forced sales pushed Bitcoin through $70,000 in about two hours overnight.

The mood has flipped with it. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index dropped from 28 to 20 on Friday, its first Extreme Fear reading since July.

In Bitcoin news this week, the question is no longer whether the market is scared. It is whether Extreme Fear means the bottom is close, and what the daily and weekly charts say.

The slide started on Thursday afternoon, when Nvidia announced that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned. It picked up speed after midnight UTC, when Bitcoin broke below the $72,727 low from Tuesday and kept falling.

We added up every forced closure in Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP and Dogecoin futures on OKX, one of the largest exchanges, over the past 24 hours.

Investors have also kept pulling money from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, funds that buy and hold the coin itself, adding to the selling.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $72,700 as Leveraged Traders Buy the Dip: Is the Bottom In?

On Thursday, we listed three signs that would point to a bottom: the fear index dropping toward the teens, the funding rate turning negative and open interest, the value of open futures bets, falling as longs give up. Overnight, two of them showed up.

One sign still points the other way. On OKX, 3.19 accounts are long for every one that is short, about the same as before the crash. Many traders are still buying the dip with leverage.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Extreme Fear sounds like a buy signal. History says it usually comes early. We found every time since 2018 that the index first dropped to 20 or lower after at least a month without such a reading. There were 16, and we followed Bitcoin for 90 days after each.

The most recent case fits the pattern. Extreme Fear first appeared on June 3 at $64,014, and Bitcoin still fell another 8.5% before it bottomed at $57,800 on July 1. Then it rallied to $87,396 in September.

For anyone reading this Bitcoin news as a buy signal, Extreme Fear says the bottom is getting closer. It has rarely said the bottom is here. A move to the 2026 lows would match the median path.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, Bitcoin sits far below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight. The 50-day EMA is at $78,226 and the 200-day EMA at $76,325.

On the weekly chart, where each candle covers one week, the key level is the 200-week EMA at $69,555. Bitcoin trades just below it, and the week closes on Sunday.

That line matters. Bitcoin closed below the 200-week EMA for 16 weeks this year, in February and March and again from June to mid-August, and both of 2026’s bottoms formed during those stretches.

The overnight flush did part of the work a bottom needs: leverage came out and funding turned negative.

For traders following Bitcoin news, the Sunday weekly close against $69,555 is the next test. History says the final low often comes weeks after the first Extreme Fear reading.

#5137. Ethlabs Calls for Ethereum Quantum Protection in 2027 as Upgrade Priorities Shift

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Ethlabs proposes quantum readiness in 2027 and plans to withdraw its quick-slots work from Hegotá. Developers still need to agree on the network's priorities.

Ethereum's next upgrade debate is becoming a question of how much engineering effort should move toward long-term security. In a November 11 proposal, Ethlabs argues for making quantum protection and resilience against advanced AI-assisted attacks the priority for 2027.

The practical question is which improvements can share an upgrade without slowing the security work. That trade-off deserves attention even from readers who never run a validator: protocol roadmaps influence the software that wallets, exchanges and applications must eventually support.

Ethlabs distinguishes basic readiness from full performance: keeping Ethereum operational with quantum-safe options is the main objective, while matching full network capacity is the more ambitious goal. Its proposed reshuffle includes withdrawing quick slots from Hegotá and reconsidering work outside that security objective.

This is a contribution to Ethereum's development process. A research group's preferred date does not establish an activation date, and an architectural direction still needs specifications, implementations and testing. The useful evidence from here will be what client teams agree to build and what they can demonstrate together.

NewsBTC's earlier coverage of Ethereum's proposed base-layer reconstruction helps explain why changes to speed, security and account design have become closely connected.

One relevant building block is EIP-8141, the frame-transaction proposal. It would let a transaction contain separate steps for validation, fee approval and execution. The design gives accounts more flexibility over how they authorise activity, including a path away from today's elliptic-curve signatures.

It also provides for key rotation, batched operations and alternative fee payment. Those features matter because a cryptographic migration is easier to manage when an account's identity can survive a change in its authorisation method.

That creates an important implementation question. An upgrade can enable a safer signature scheme, but wallet developers still have to expose it clearly, exchanges have to recognise it, and users need a recovery path that they understand. Flexibility in the protocol only becomes useful protection when the surrounding software makes it usable.

Ethereum's quantum-security overview identifies multiple areas of exposure: ordinary account signatures, validator signatures, data commitments and some proof systems. Each has a different role, so replacing one component would leave other migration work outstanding.

The same overview says present-day quantum computers cannot break Ethereum's cryptography. Preparation is being undertaken because a transition across a large network takes time, while future hardware capability is uncertain. Hash-based approaches are among the routes being researched, with different efficiency and deployment challenges from current systems.

The distinction between a future cryptographic threat and an active compromise is essential. Readers should not interpret a more ambitious research timetable as evidence that current Ethereum accounts have suddenly been broken. NewsBTC has previously examined Justin Drake's view of quantum migration as a broader redesign opportunity.

Our reading is that the proposal's significance lies in resource allocation. Every additional feature creates implementation and review work, while concentrating on security can defer improvements that other users want sooner. Neither choice is costless.

A credible programme therefore needs measurable milestones: working clients, agreement on migration behaviour and evidence about performance under the new cryptography. It also needs a clear account of which guarantees are available at each stage.

For ETH holders, those milestones will be more informative than a calendar target alone. The debate now asks developers to turn an ambitious security objective into a sequence that the wider Ethereum ecosystem can actually deliver.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

#5136. Dogecoin ETFs Mark One Month of Zero Activity

As Dogecoin continues to struggle amid prolonged crypto market volatility, its ETF performance has remained muted for the past week, drawing attention from market participants.

Although Dogecoin has retained its position as the king of all meme tokens, institutional demand for the leading meme token has remained on hold as it continues to post deeper price corrections.

Latest data from SosoValue shows that the U.S. Dogecoin spot ETFs have gone an entire month without recording any new inflows or outflows.

More specifically, the two existing spot DOGE ETFs last recorded activity on October 13, when they experienced a combined net outflow of $138,570.

The ETFs became muted the following day, October 14, and neither of the funds has registered a single day of positive or negative flows since then, leaving daily net inflows at zero until November 13.

As such, the Dogecoin ETFs have posted zero flows all month, signaling fading institutional interest in the world’s largest meme token by market capitalization despite its leading position in the memecoin market.

While institutional interest in Dogecoin appears to have declined significantly, both Dogecoin ETF issuers, Grayscale and 21Shares, recorded zero daily net inflows on November 13, confirming that the prolonged period of inactivity remains unchanged.

However, Grayscale's Dogecoin ETF has retained its dominance in the U.S. spot Dogecoin ETF market, holding a total of $9.15 million in net assets, while 21Shares' Dogecoin ETF has held only $1.58 million since its launch.

As such, Grayscale accounts for about 85.3% of the combined $10.73 million in assets held across the Dogecoin ETF market.

#5135. TRON, Tether and Chainalysis launch task force as crypto hacks hit $8.78B

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

On the 12th of November, TRON, Tether, and blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis jointly launched the Digital Crime Task Force (DCTF), an initiative aimed at identifying and disrupting illicit financial activities involving Tether’s USDT stablecoin on the TRON blockchain.

In this plan, TRON will contribute its blockchain network expertise, and Tether will provide support as the issuer of USDT. Meanwhile, Chainalysis will bring its blockchain intelligence, investigative expertise, and AI-powered monitoring tools.

One of the major reasons behind the initiative is the growing sophistication of crypto-related financial crime. According to Chainalysis, AI-enabled scam operations were 4.5x more profitable than traditional scams in 2025. Meanwhile, impersonation scams increased by more than 1,400% year over year.

DefiLlama further reported that the crypto industry recorded $8.78 billion across 328 hacks in 2026 so far. This is the highest annual loss recorded in its database. In fact, the five biggest hacks together contributed more than 85% of the overall losses.

Interestingly, the number of attacks increased around 2.7 times compared to 2025, while the median loss declined from $1.07 million to $510,000. This suggests that hackers are carrying out more frequent attacks, although most incidents involve relatively smaller amounts.

Seeing this rise, the organizations believe that traditional approaches, which often depend on victims reporting crimes or investigators identifying suspicious funds, are no longer sufficient. Instead, they want to identify potential threats before criminals can move their funds.

Remarking on the same, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said,

Criminals are using AI to move faster than ever, and waiting for a victim to report a crime is no longer good enough

This remark comes as Tether has already frozen more than $7 billion linked to illicit activities while working with over 360 law enforcement agencies across 73 countries.

That said, the new task force will therefore be built on these efforts by focusing on proactive investigations and faster coordination. It will also accept tips and asset-freezing requests directly from law enforcement agencies.

Needless to say, the DCTF will investigate several categories of financial crime, including investment and romance scams, stolen funds, cryptocurrency hacks, terrorist financing, North Korean cyber operations, and much more.

This coincided with the FBI recently launching ‘Operation Blackout,’ a coordinated international crackdown targeting scam compounds across Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Middle East that defraud American citizens through fake investment platforms and online impersonation.

Meanwhile, ACAMS has partnered with blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis to strengthen cryptocurrency anti-financial crime training through an updated CCAS certification.
